newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania to liberalise copper exports.
newsitem.headline: Romania to liberalise copper exports.

text.p: Romania, an associate member of the European Community, will fully liberalise copper exports next week in a move to adapt to the EU internal market, a senior official said on Friday.
"The government decision to liberalise copper exports will come into force next Monday," said Ion Capota, Industry Ministry director in charge of the metallurgical sector.
Copper exports have been banned to date.
Capota said the ministry expected a copper output of some 30,000 tonnes this year. Copper production amounted to 28,300 tonnes in 1996, data show.
Last year, Romania set export quotas for copper-zinc alloys at 1,000 tonnes and for copper-tin alloys to 3,000 tonnes.
The move to liberalise copper exports is part of Romania's strategy to adapt to the EU internal market, in view of its possible membership.
